newsitem.title: POLAND: CU Polish unit 1996 premiums rise 168 pct.
newsitem.headline: CU Polish unit 1996 premiums rise 168 pct.

text.p: Gross premiums gained by the Polish life insurance unit of British Commercial Union Plc (CU) rose last year by 168 percent to 320 million zlotys and were seen rising to 500 million in 1997, the unit's president said.
"We had 320 (million zlotys) last year...and (the premiums should rise) to 500 million in 1997 -- that's about a 50-percent increase," Marian Miziolek told Reuters after a news conference on Tuesday.
Miziolek said the company had raised its market share to 11.5 percent in 1996 and should raise it to between 12 and 13 percent this year.
He told the news conference that the firm had increased its number of clients in 1996 by 198,000 to 457,000 while the net value of its participation units grew by 24 percent.

Miziolek was speaking at a news conference on the firm's introduction of a universal insurance policy for youth, of which he said the firm would probably sell about 10,000 this year, five percent of its overall number of policy sales.
He said the firm sought to begin annuities and a variety of investment funds later this year.
Commercial Union Towarzystwo Ubezpieczen na Zycie Polska SA is 90-percent owned by British CU and 10-percent by Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy SA (WBK).
It ranks second among Polish life insurers after Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen (PZU) Zycie, a subsidary of the non-life state-owned PZU. PZU Life has about an 80 percent market share.
In the first three quarters of last year the CU Polish unit collected 212.2 million zlotys in gross premiums and made a net profit of 15.8 million zlotys.
In the whole of 1995 it had 119.5 million zlotys in gross premiums and netted 6.8 million.
